decided: The shipped exporters' spelling becomes the outcome event's one canonical wire format, defined once as exported constants that every exporter and querier uses instead of the 63 string literals scattered across them today. ADR-0002's canonical JSON and docs/semconv.md are corrected to that spelling rather than the code being changed to theirs. An outcome-event conformance vector lands under testkit/vectors/, the treatment the codec and registry already get, and a testkit assertion drives every exporter through it so the field names are checked rather than described. biz.sla.deadline is added to the CloudWatch and GCP events so all three transports emit the same fields from the same Outcome, which is what ADR-0002 already claims; OTLP's trace handling stays as native span context and the vector records that as a declared transport difference rather than a mismatch.
why: The event is the product's public wire format — the thing a user's downstream actually reads — and it is spelled three ways: ADR-0002 says flow/entity_id/amount_minor/kind/est, semconv.md says biz.flow/biz.entity_id/biz.money.amount_minor/biz.kind/biz.estimated, and the shipped exporters emit biz.flow/biz.entity.id/biz.amount_minor/biz.value.kind/biz.amount.est. Two ports and any external adapter author have to pick one, and picking creates a fourth. The exporters win because they are what every current consumer reads, what the gcplogging querier already parses back with JSON paths, and because all three of them already agree with each other exactly — the disagreement is entirely between the code and its documentation, so correcting the docs changes no bytes on any wire. Constants rather than literals is the part that stops this recurring: drift was not a mistake someone made, it was the default state of a contract that existed only as repeated strings with nothing tying them together. ADR-0002 also claims a testkit conformance test asserts both transports produce the same fields; no such test exists, and the transports do not in fact agree — biz.sla.deadline is emitted by OTLP alone. That is the gap that let the spellings diverge, and closing it is what makes the ADR's own promise true.
cost_if_wrong: Freezing the shipped spelling freezes its inconsistency: biz.amount.est sits under an amount. namespace that biz.amount_minor does not use, and biz.entity.id is dotted where biz.amount_minor is flat. Pre-1.0 is the cheap moment to rename and this decision declines to take it, so a later rename costs a major version or a compatibility shim. That is deliberate — a wire-format rename is the founder's call and does not belong inside a settlement PR — and it is filed separately rather than smuggled in. Adding biz.sla.deadline to two exporters puts a field on every CloudWatch and GCP event that nothing in this library reads back; if that is unwanted the cheaper correction is to drop it from OTLP instead, which is a one-line change in the other direction. The constants are exported API, so their names are themselves a contract.
alternatives: Adopt semconv.md's spelling (biz.money.amount_minor, biz.entity_id) — rejected: it is a draft proposal, it disagrees with every shipped exporter and with the gcplogging querier's JSON paths, and adopting it changes the bytes on three live wires to settle a documentation disagreement

Adopt ADR-0002's canonical JSON (bare flow, entity_id, est) — rejected: those names are unnamespaced, so they collide with any other producer writing to the same event sink, which is the reason the biz. prefix exists

Redesign the scheme properly while settling it (biz.amount.minor, biz.amount.currency, biz.amount.estimated) — rejected for this PR: it is the internally consistent scheme and probably the right long-term answer, but it changes three exporters, two queriers and the goldens at the same moment as the settlement, and a settlement that also relitigates the design is how a contract fix turns into a multi-round rewrite. Filed for the founder to weigh on its own

Leave biz.sla.deadline emitted by OTLP only and record it in the vector as a transport difference — rejected: ADR-0002 states the transports produce the same fields, and a vector that encodes a known inconsistency as correct enshrines the defect it was added to prevent. Removing it from OTLP instead is the live alternative if adding it is judged wrong

Constants in a new package rather than in biz or emit — rejected: the names describe biz.Outcome's own fields, so they belong with the type they name; a third package for eleven strings is indirection without a boundary
scope: New exported attribute-name constants and the replacement of the 63 non-test literals across adapters/export/{cloudwatch,gcp,otlp} and adapters/query/gcplogging. biz.sla.deadline added to the CloudWatch and GCP event builders. A new outcome-event vector under testkit/vectors/ plus the testkit assertion that drives each exporter through it. ADR-0002 amended for the spelling and for its false claim about an existing conformance test; docs/semconv.md corrected. No change to biz.Outcome, biz.ValueContext, the emit interfaces, the metric families, or the engine's read path — this settles how the event is spelled on the wire, not what it contains.
